India Metals & Mining Sector Posts Steady Growth in Q4, Driven by Domestic Demand

India’s metals and mining sector recorded a stable performance in the fourth quarter, buoyed by robust domestic demand and an uptick in infrastructure spending. According to data released Thursday by the Federation of Indian Mineral Industries, aggregate quarterly revenues for listed miners rose 5.8% year-on-year to ₹1.46 trillion, while net profits climbed 4.3% to ₹172 billion.

The sector’s growth was underpinned by strong steel and aluminum sales, both of which benefited from government-led infrastructure projects and resilient auto sector demand. Steel output rose 3.6% to 33.2 million tonnes, while aluminum production was up 2.9% at 1.2 million tonnes for the quarter.

“We are seeing consistent offtake from construction, railways, and renewable energy segments,” said Manish Agarwal, CFO of Suryodaya Metals, one of India’s leading producers. “The government’s ongoing focus on infrastructure is a key driver for the industry.”

Mining output also rose modestly, with iron ore production up 4.1% and coal output increasing 3.4%, as reported by the Indian Bureau of Mines. The sector’s performance was further supported by stable commodity prices and improved logistics, with the easing of port congestion in the eastern states.

Analysts noted that margins for most companies remained healthy despite higher input costs. “Domestic demand has largely offset global price volatility and input inflation,” said Gauri Shah, metals analyst at Mumbai-based research firm Capital Insight. “We expect the sector to maintain steady growth in the coming quarters, provided demand from core sectors continues.”

The industry’s workforce remained stable, with no significant changes in employment levels reported during the quarter. Industry officials highlighted ongoing investments in technology and sustainability, with several companies adopting cleaner production techniques.

Looking ahead, executives and analysts anticipate continued momentum, driven by India’s capital expenditure cycle and ongoing urbanization. “We are optimistic about the sector’s outlook for the next fiscal year,” said Agarwal, “as long as the domestic growth story remains intact.”
